description: A director of regulatory affairs must approve an assurance-of-voluntary-compliance filing to a state attorney general concerning the company's automatic-renewal practices, including customer remediation, monitoring, contract changes, and liability language, with input from consumer-protection counsel, product counsel, and insurance counsel.

shared_context.S1: The state attorney general has proposed resolving a consumer-protection inquiry into the company's automatic-renewal practices through an assurance-of-voluntary-compliance filing.
shared_context.S2: The current draft requires the company to describe its remediation program but does not specify the final customer-remedy numbers, contract-flow settings, monitoring period, or liability language.
shared_context.S3: Maya Chen has final authority to approve the filing package before it is submitted.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's ordinary filing protocol, Maya conducts a recorded pre-submission review in which consumer-protection, product, and insurance counsel each report their recommendations before she approves the package.

PF1.text: Jordan completed a reconciliation of the customer account records after the draft circulated and confirmed that exactly 1,240 customers must receive refunds totaling exactly $186,000; the proposed remediation also requires an independent compliance monitor for exactly 18 months. Jordan has not yet amended the draft's unspecified remedy language.

PF2.text: In this week's product-approval conversation, the business approved a customer-protection design that lets customers cancel at any time and requires a renewal notice exactly 30 days before each renewal; preserving those two settings is the product team's non-monetary priority, but the settings are not yet in the filing draft.

PF3.text: Victor's review of the applicable insurance endorsement confirmed that written insurer consent must be obtained before issuing the refund program because its aggregate value exceeds $100,000, and the assurance filing must contain no admission of liability for coverage to remain available; these conditions have not been added to the filing checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The filing must provide refunds to exactly 1,240 customers.
The total refund amount must be exactly $186,000.
The filing must require an independent compliance monitor for exactly 18 months.
The customer contract flow must allow cancellation at any time.
The customer contract flow must provide renewal notice exactly 30 days before renewal.
Written insurer consent must be obtained before issuing the refunds.
The filing must contain no admission of liability.
The package must include a customer-refund commitment.
The package must include an independent-monitor commitment.
The reconciled customer-record finding must be cited as a justification.

decisive_facts.why: The reconciled records change the filing from unspecified remediation to exactly 1,240 refunds totaling $186,000 and exactly 18 months of independent monitoring, requiring both corresponding commitments and citation of that reconciliation.
The product team's approved design changes the contract flow from unspecified renewal controls to cancellation at any time and renewal notice exactly 30 days before renewal.
The insurance endorsement changes the filing to require written insurer consent before the $186,000 refund program and to contain no admission of liability.
